class_config.name: serial_peripheral_protocol
class_config.description: v0.1.77 — for SPI / I2C / UART / I2S / 1-Wire / CAN / SMBus / Microwire and similar synchronous-or-asynchronous serial peripheral SPEC documents. Distinguished by a small fixed external pin count (typically 2-4) carrying named functions (data/clock/select), master/slave (or controller/target) roles, a shift register as the core data-movement primitive, and clock-divisor / baud-rate control. No multi-channel handshake (that's bus_interconnect_protocol) and no SW-visible opcode protocol (that's digital_cmd_driven). L4 register map IS present (configuration register file at the host-bus interface); L5 (analog), L11 (OTP), L13 (lab cal) typically N/A. L14-L18 (versioning, encoding tables, compliance rules, channel catalog, interconnect rules) all apply to the serial protocol layer. Phase 2 runner dispatches via fallback_skill=spec-to-rtl since the spec is a wire-level protocol, not a complete IC.
